not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

sampling context together.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Prednisolone, which shares the query's 1,4-dien-3-one/11β-hydroxy/21-hydroxy corticosteroid core, has an average absolute oral bioavailability of about 70% in humans and high intestinal permeability (Peff 4.4×10^-4 cm/s; fraction absorbed 95%), showing that the corticosteroid scaffold can meet F≥20% even when it is a P-gp/CYP3A4 substrate.

Hydrocortisone records show high intestinal permeability dominated by passive diffusion, and corticosteroid P-gp efflux is inhibitable; gut-wall efflux and intestinal metabolism alone do not establish F<20%.

The prior low prediction relied mainly on beclomethasone dipropionate (a 17,21-diester prodrug) and estradiol, which are less structurally transferable to the query's 21-hydroxy 16,17-acetal corticosteroid; their low oral Cmax/exposure is not affirmative evidence that des-CIC has F<20%.

Multiple steroid reference contexts show high oral bioavailability for steroid scaffolds (digitoxin 90.6%, β-methyldigoxin 59–76%, danazol 46–67%, ethinylestradiol 76.9%), supporting the plausibility of high oral F for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query or des-CIC.
No oral F record for a 16,17-acetal corticosteroid is visible; transfer from prednisolone/hydrocortisone to the acetal is uncertain.
Acid lability of the 16,17-acetal and the extent of first-pass metabolism for the query are not experimentally quantified.
Formulation, dose, and prandial state for the query are unspecified.
P-gp/CYP3A4 substrate status of the query itself is not directly measured.
content.decision_summary: Flipped to high: L5 provides direct evidence that corticosteroids such as prednisolone have about 70% absolute oral bioavailability and high intestinal permeability despite P-gp/CYP3A4 substrate status, and L4 shows high fraction absorbed for the corticosteroid scaffold. The prior low was based on less transferable BDP/estradiol prodrug records. The 16,17-acetal remains a structural uncertainty, so confidence is low.
